resources.string: A word you type that the dictionary did not have costs one slow spelling, once. Turn this off and it costs that every time. Passwords and fields that ask not to be learnt from are never remembered, whatever this says.
Everything the keyboard learnt, and where to remove any of it.
The language switch cycles through the ones you tick, in this order.
At least one language has to stay on.

Remotes disagree about which buttons exist and about what they report. Press the button you want and it gets recorded. Only the first is worth assigning on most remotes: spelling is also a held number key, deleting is BACK while a word is in progress, and the language switch does nothing with one language on. Number keys cannot be assigned — they are the keyboard.
In use. Focus a text field and it comes up.
Enabled, but another keyboard is in use. Switch to this one below.
Not enabled yet. Android needs every keyboard turned on by hand — do that below, then switch to it.
Leaves this app. Enable or switch the active keyboard there.
The only thing here that uses the network. It runs in a separate process, only when you press it, and sends nothing. What you type never leaves the device.

Number keys carry the letters, one press each — 2 for a, b or c, and the dictionary works out which you meant. Polish accents come free: press 9 for ż, 6 for ó, and the word arrives spelled properly.

Left and right walk the words the presses could mean. Centre finishes the word, 0 finishes it and adds a space, 1 cycles the punctuation a search box needs.

When nothing matches, the strip says so. Hold any number key to spell the word out letter by letter — that costs a few presses once, and the word is kept, so the next time it is one press per letter like everything else.

BACK drops a word in progress, then closes the keyboard.
Focus this field to bring the keyboard up. Nothing here is saved, and nothing typed here is learnt.
Press the key that should open the keyboard when it is hidden.
Without this the keyboard only appears when an app asks for it, which Netflix and YouTube do not always do.
Press the key that should switch to spelling letter by letter.
Also reachable by holding 1, which the grid on the keyboard says.
Press the key that should delete.
BACK already deletes while a word is in progress.
Press the key that should change language.
Only useful with more than one language enabled.
The keyboard needs this button for typing, so it cannot be assigned. Choose again and press a different one.
The next button you press is the one taken. BACK cancels.
Added when you type a word the dictionary did not have. Nothing here has ever left this device.
No word for these keys — hold 1 to spell it once and it is kept.
No dictionary for this language: only spelling works.
Nothing here takes text. Open a search box first.
This field asked not to be learnt from, so nothing typed here is kept.
Shows the number keys and the letters on each. The remote has nothing printed on it, so leave this on until you know the layout.
Just the candidates and the state line. Assumes you know which key carries which letters.
The smallest strip there is, leaving the most room for what is underneath.
T9 is open source and MIT licensed. It is free, it stays free, and nothing in it is locked away for people who do not pay.
If it has saved you a few thousand trips around an on-screen grid, you can buy me a coffee.
Press the key that should switch between letters and digits.
A field that wants a number switches on its own, so this is only for typing a number into an ordinary field.
T9 installs from its GitHub releases.
This repository has no releases yet.
Handing the file to the system installer.
Android stops an app when it replaces it, so this screen will close. The keyboard itself keeps working — reopen the app only to change settings.
The system asked for confirmation but did not say what to show.
Android needs your permission for this app to install packages.
Checked only when you press it. One request for the version, one for the file, nothing sent. What you type never leaves the device.
